review_candidates.title: Senior Supply Chain Associate
review_candidates.description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates. Organizational Context and Scope Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) or Head of Office (HoO) and direct supervision of the Supply Chain Officer, the Senior Supply Chain Associate will be support the supply chain officer in day to day supply chain activities, guided by Supply Chain Management (SCM) objectives to deliver quality goods/services to the beneficiaries at optimal price and in a timely manner. Responsibilities Carry out and support coordination of procurement activities in the office, including revision and consolidation of purchase request forms, organization and evaluation of bidding processes and follow up on purchase orders until the successful delivery of the products or services and timely payment to suppliers. Assist supervisors in more complex, higher-value purchases. Support the development of procurement plans to optimize purchasing power and facilitate the implementation of project activities. Participate in negotiations of terms and conditions of purchases and help resolve issues related to the delivery of goods and services. Provide technical guidance to requisitioners and all staff in the office on preparation of specifications and procurement instructions and procedures. Participate in the development, evaluation, and updating of systems and procedures for procurement; suggest areas for improvement and risk-mitigation measures. Identify local and international suppliers and service providers; participate in their evaluation taking into consideration quality, prices, reliability, and services and the organization’s best interests. Contribute to the development of tools for tracking of contracts, agreements, and progress toward the achievement of the procurement plans and schedules. Coordinate the maintenance of files with all required documentation and the preparation and timely submission of reports and statistics. Provide specialized support in the planning, implementation and monitoring of supply chain activities related to property and asset management, warehousing, insurance coverage, maintenance, and transportation. Coordinate supply chain operations with other UN Agencies, partners, and government authorities. Plan and coordinate fleet activities of the office and monitor fuel consumption and maintenance of vehicles. Coordinate service and maintenance of office facilities and equipment and a continued supply of all essential utilities and items used in the office. Provide training and guidance to the junior SCM staff of CO, while supervising, monitoring, evaluating and supporting their professional and career development. Participate and engage actively in the UN inter-agency meetings and forums related to supply chain management. Collaborate on sharing resources to achieve common goals and implementation of UN global initiatives. Perform other duties as may be assigned. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education University degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Logistics, Supply Chain Management or a related field from an accredited academic institution with four years of relevant professional experience; or High school diploma with six years of relevant professional experience Certification in Procurement, Logistics or Supply Chain Management is an advantage Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Experience in procurement and logistics and working with service providers and vendors; Experience with asset management process; Experience working with IOM/UN Procurement and Logistics Rules and Procedures is an advantage; Experience working in an international organization in a multi-cultural setting an advantage; Experience in training and coordinating teams. Skills High level of computer literacy; Ability to work with national and international institutions; Ability to prepare clear and concise report; Demonstrated ability to and exercise sound judgment; Ability to supervise staff and coordinate administrative activities; Excellent communication and negotiation skills; Ability to establish realistic resource requirements to meet IOM needs. Languages All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish). For this position, fluency in English & Portuguese is required (oral and written). Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Required Competencies IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link . Competencies will be assessed during the selection process. Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values: Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion. Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct. Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance. Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated. Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2 Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results. Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes. Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate. Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work. Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way. Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2, if with direct reports Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential. Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty. Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction. Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings. Notes Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months. Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances. IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities. IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts. IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here ). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application. No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

review_candidates.title: Senior Programme Manager
review_candidates.description: Job Highlight Providing strategic leadership and oversight of monitoring, evaluation, reporting and learning across Global Fund-supported health programmes to ensure credible performance evidence, strong data quality, effective programme accountability and evidence-based decision-making. About The Project Office The Asia Regional Health Cluster (ARHC) is a dedicated UNOPS unit focused on delivering health programmes and procurement across the Asia Pacific region. Headquartered in Bangkok, Thailand, ARHC operates through a network of personnel in UNOPS country offices, leveraging local support services. ARHC's mission is to improve health outcomes and contribute to SDG 3 by providing tailored solutions and advisory services. Its expertise encompasses programme and fund management, pharmaceuticals and health sector procurement, and technical expertise in the health sector. Since 2011, ARHC has managed over US$1.68 billion in Global Fund grants for HIV, TB, and malaria programmes in the Greater Mekong Subregion, supporting national programmes, NGOs, and multilateral organizations. ARHC also extends its capabilities and services to UNOPS multi-country and country offices in the region, promoting regional collaboration and impact in the health sector. Role Purpose The Senior Programme Manager (M&E) provides strategic leadership, technical direction and managerial oversight for monitoring, evaluation, reporting, data quality and learning across UNOPS-managed Global Fund-supported programmes. The role establishes and assures a consistent portfolio-wide M&E architecture while enabling fit-to-context arrangements for HIV, malaria, tuberculosis and regional grants. The incumbent leads and supervises the Monitoring and Evaluation Specialists, sets priorities and quality standards, reviews and clears key deliverables, and ensures that programme evidence is timely, credible and used for management decisions. The role advises senior management on programme trajectories, performance risks, grant ratings and corrective actions; maintains effective engagement with the Global Fund, Local Fund Agent, National Programmes, Co-Principal Recipients, Sub-Recipients and technical partners; and promotes responsible adoption of digital health, analytics and interoperable information systems. Functions / Key Results Expected Under the direct supervision of the Head of Principal Recipient Global Fund Management, the Senior Programme Manager (M&E) is accountable for the strategic direction, management and quality assurance of the M&E function across the assigned grant portfolio. The incumbent will perform, but not be limited to, the following responsibilities: Strategic M&E Leadership and Governance Lead the development and periodic revision of portfolio and grant-level M&E strategies, Performance Frameworks, monitoring plans, indicator guidance, reporting protocols and standard operating procedures. Contribute to the development and updating of national disease M&E plans, ensuring that UNOPS systems are coherent with national systems and responsive to evolving programme and donor requirements. Establish fit-to-context M&E arrangements that reflect grant, disease, geographic, access and implementation realities while maintaining consistent portfolio-wide quality standards. Advise senior management on programme performance, grant ratings, data limitations, emerging risks and corrective actions. Oversee responsible adoption of digital M&E dashboards, predictive analytics and other technological tools, ensuring appropriate data protection, sustainability and partner ownership. Lead the grant negotiations for M&E including submission of quality inputs required to ensure the grant agreement signature. Team Leadership and Quality Assurance Lead and supervise M&E Specialists supporting HIV, tuberculosis, malaria and regional grants, ensuring clear accountabilities, coordinated workplans, balanced workloads and effective cross-grant collaboration. Set team and individual objectives, provide technical guidance and coaching, review performance and identify professional-development and resourcing needs. Review and clear key M&E products, particularly high-risk or externally submitted deliverables, to ensure technical accuracy, consistency, traceability and compliance. Foster an inclusive, accountable and learning-oriented team culture that promotes collaboration, innovation and staff wellbeing. Monitoring, Reporting and Performance Management Direct the implementation and continuous improvement of monitoring and reporting systems across the portfolio, ensuring timely submission of structured and quality-assured data by National Programmes, Co-PRs, SRs and implementing partners. Oversee maintenance of the M&E database and related repositories, ensuring incoming data are validated, securely managed and readily available for authorized analysis and reporting. Ensure timely preparation and quality assurance of PUDRs, Pulse Checks, grant performance reports, quarterly, annual and ad hoc progress updates, management reports and presentations. Review overall grant and indicator performance against approved targets and cumulative results, identifying trends, variances, implementation gaps and actions required to improve performance. Coordinate responses to Global Fund, Local Fund Agent and management queries and maintain a consolidated calendar of reporting obligations, reviews and evaluations. Data Quality, Assurance and Performance Analysis Establish and oversee a risk-based assurance framework and M&E workplan covering data-quality assessments, data verification, programmatic spot checks, field monitoring and follow-up of findings. Direct or commission data audits, verification exercises and spot checks at national and subnational levels, ensuring that findings and corrective actions are properly documented and tracked. Review and validate M&E findings produced by National Programmes and SRs and ensure follow-up of agreed recommendations. Oversee reconciliation of programmatic results with financial implementation, procurement and supply data, escalating material discrepancies and recurrent issues. Lead portfolio-level qualitative and quantitative analysis, including variance analysis, dashboards, scorecards and predictive approaches, to support management decisions and anticipate implementation bottlenecks. Digital M&E Systems, Data Governance and Advanced Analytics Provide strategic leadership and oversight for the development, integration and continuous improvement of databases, electronic information systems, digital health platforms and other technology-enabled M&E solutions across the grant portfolio. Direct the development and use of real-time digital dashboards, automated reporting tools and interactive data visualizations to strengthen portfolio oversight, enable early identification of performance issues and support timely management decisions. Promote the use of advanced data analytics, including trend, variance, geospatial and predictive analysis, to assess programme trajectories, anticipate implementation bottlenecks and inform corrective action and resource prioritization. Establish and oversee data-governance arrangements covering data quality, ownership, access, security, privacy, retention, documentation and responsible use. Promote interoperability, standardized indicators, metadata management, version control and effective information exchange between UNOPS, national and partner systems. Review and approve proposed digital tools and system enhancements, ensuring fitness for purpose, compatibility, sustainability, value for money and avoidance of unnecessary duplication. Provide strategic oversight and coordination of UNOPS support to relevant Ministry of Health e-health and digital health initiatives, including DHIS/DHIS2, the Master Patient Index and other national platforms, and ensure effective monitoring and reporting of activities financed by the Global Fund. Technical Support, Evaluation and Capacity Strengthening Provide high-level technical guidance to National Programmes, Co-PRs, SRs and implementing partners on M&E methodologies, indicators, surveillance, reporting, data management and programme performance. Guide M&E inputs to grant-making, grant negotiations, implementation planning, workplan and budget reviews, reprogramming, portfolio optimization, performance assessments and grant closure. Lead or coordinate UNOPS participation in technical reviews, programme evaluations, surveys, operational assessments and special studies, ensuring methodological quality and practical use of findings. Support the Ministry of Health and National Programmes to strengthen M&E and surveillance systems, including appropriate sentinel surveillance mechanisms for monitoring programme outcomes and impact. Set the strategic direction for partner capacity development and approve training, mentoring and digital-upskilling plans, guidance documents and job aids. Ensure capacity-strengthening support improves partner reporting, data quality, evidence use, health-service delivery and implementation of approved programme plans. Coordination, Knowledge Management and Learning Lead M&E coordination with Programme Management, Finance, Procurement and Supply Chain Management, Compliance and other relevant functions to support integrated programme oversight. Maintain effective relationships with the Global Fund Country Team, LFA, National Programmes, Co-PRs, SRs, CCM/CDW structures, WHO, UN agencies, civil society and development partners. Chair or facilitate programme performance reviews, data-review sessions and M&E coordination forums, ensuring clear decisions, assigned actions and timely follow-up. Represent UNOPS in technical and strategic meetings, grant review missions, evaluations and donor discussions, presenting consolidated updates on programme performance, risks and corrective actions. Promote an active learning culture and oversee the documentation, storage and dissemination of scientific evidence, technical guidance, lessons learned, good practices and innovations. Facilitate cross-grant learning and ensure monitoring and evaluation findings inform programme adaptation, strategic planning and resource prioritization. Compliance, Audit and Risk Management Ensure M&E and reporting arrangements comply with Global Fund requirements, UNOPS policies, applicable national guidance, donor standards and relevant data-protection obligations. Maintain oversight of portfolio-level M&E risks and ensure that proportionate mitigation measures are implemented and material risks escalated. Lead M&E support to internal and external audits, LFA reviews, technical-assistance missions and programme evaluations. Ensure recommendations arising from audits, reviews and evaluations are properly documented, assigned, followed up and closed. Promote effective document control, evidence retention, data traceability and readiness for assurance reviews. Perform other strategic M&E, programme assurance and management functions assigned by the supervisor in support of effective Global Fund grant implementation. Education Requirements Required Master’s degree or equivalent - preferably in Public Health, Epidemiology Statistics, Evaluation, Project Management, or related area is required. OR Bachelor’s Degree with a relevant combination of academic qualifications and 2 additional years experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Required Experience Requirements A minimum of 7 years of monitoring and evaluation experience in health programmes. Successful development and implementation of an M&E system at programme level. Familiarity with DHIS2 (District Health Information Software) or similar integrated public health databases and technological tools. Prior experience working with donors/ multi-donor funds. Willingness to undertake field visits in difficult conditions. Experience in the usage of computers and office software packages (MS Office 2010 and/or newer versions). Desired Previous work in and knowledge of the political, economic and social situation in Myanmar. Sound knowledge of UNOPS regulations and rules. Ability to analyze large datasets using software such as Stata, SPSS, R, or Python. Familiarity with mobile data collection tools like KoBoToolbox, ODK (Open Data Kit), or CommCare for field-level health data gathering.

review_candidates.description: Czym się zajmujemy? W Eternis zmieniamy zasady gry w branży mobility & delivery. Tworzymy operacje i systemy, które mają realny wpływ na sposób, w jaki się dziś zarabia i pracuje w branży ride-hailing i delivery. Zarządzamy nowoczesną flotą, rozwijamy operacje taxi i delivery w wielu miastach w Polsce i za granicą oraz budujemy własne narzędzia technologiczne, które codziennie wspierają tysiące kierowców i kurierów na każdym etapie współpracy - od onboardingu, przez codzienne operacje, aż po rozliczenia,w bliskiej współpracy z globalnymi platformami takimi jak Uber, Bolt, Glovo, Wolt, Uber Eats czy i FREE NOW. Jeśli chcesz działać w środowisku, które wyznacza nowe standardy, daje przestrzeń na rozwój i pozwala realnie zmieniać branżę, jesteś we właściwym miejscu. Co wyróżnia tę rolę? Eternis to dziś ponad 12 000 aktywnych klientów i 1000+ aut we flocie - bardzo zróżnicowana społeczność kierowców i kurierów działających w gig economy. To skala, która wymaga nie tylko sprawnej obsługi, ale prawdziwego systemu: powtarzalnego, opartego na procesie, mierzalnego i zbudowanego pod wzrost. Szukamy osoby, która przyjmie pełną odpowiedzialność za operacyjne prowadzenie segmentu taxi w Polsce. Jako Senior Operations Leader (Taxi) będziesz odpowiadać za wynik operacyjny, łącząc obszary Fleet, Obsługi Klienta w Oddziałach, Process Excellence, Revenue & Performance oraz operacje miejskie w Polsce. Twoim celem będzie stworzenie powtarzalnej i mierzalnej maszyny operacyjnej, która pozwoli Eternis stale zwiększać liczbę aktywnych kierowców,, jednocześnie poprawiając ekonomikę jednostkową. Jakie zadania na Ciebie czekają? Jako Senior Operations Leader (Taxi) będziesz odpowiedzialny/a za: Całościowy wynik biznesowy segmentu taxi w Polsce: liczbę aktywnych kierowców, retencję, realizację targetów oraz poziom churnu. Definiowanie i realizację strategii rozwoju segmentu taxi w Polsce, przekładanie priorytetów strategicznych na konkretne inicjatywy operacyjne. Zarządzanie budżetem i kosztami operacyjnymi segmentu taxi, w tym identyfikowanie obszarów optymalizacji. Zarządzanie zespołem działającym na wspólny wynik biznesowy — wyznaczanie celów, priorytetów i sposobu mierzenia sukcesu. Zbieranie i analizę danych z różnych źródeł w celu monitorowania KPI oraz bieżącego zrozumienia wyników segmentu, przekładanie wniosków na konkretne rekomendacje i plany działania. Prowadzenie cyklicznych przeglądów wyników oddziałów (Branch Performance Check) w obszarze taxi wraz z rekomendacjami usprawnień. Nadzór nad planami naprawczymi — ich zatwierdzanie, monitorowanie postępów oraz eskalację w przypadku braku skuteczności. Standaryzację procesów w segmencie taxi, we współpracy z ogólnofirmowym rejestrem procesów i narzędzi (oddziały/centrala), oraz ich dokumentowanie w celu poprawy efektywności operacyjnej. Współpracę międzyfunkcyjną z działami legalizacji, licencji, floty, księgowości, logistyki, sprzedaży, marketingu oraz zespołem technicznym w celu zapewnienia najwyższej jakości działania segmentu — budowanie porozumienia co do celów i jasną komunikację postępów, również w stronę kierownictwa. Reprezentowanie Country Managera na spotkaniach biznesowych i międzynarodowych dotyczących segmentu taxi oraz zastępowanie go pod jego nieobecność w tym zakresie. Podnoszenie standardu komunikacji z kierowcami we wszystkich platformach i kanałach (kontakt osobisty, telefoniczny, mailowy oraz media społecznościowe), z dbałością o spójne doświadczenie kierowcy niezależnie od kraju pochodzenia czy kultury. Kogo szukamy? 5+ lat doświadczenia w operacjach, w tym w strukturach rozproszonych Doświadczenie w zarządzaniu biznesem o wysokim wolumenie i dynamice Praca w środowisku operacyjnie intensywnym (mobility, logistyka last mile, fleet, marketplace, gig economy, sieć serwisowa lub retail wielooddziałowy) Udokumentowane doświadczenie w skalowaniu biznesu i budowaniu powtarzalnych procesów Bardzo dobre rozumienie danych, KPI, P&L, EBITDA i ekonomiki jednostkowej, umiejętność przekładania ich na decyzje operacyjne Doświadczenie w środowisku międzynarodowym i regulowanym; znajomość wielu języków i kultur mile widziana Postawa hands-on - nie tylko zarządzanie i delegowanie, ale też budowanie, wdrażanie i egzekwowanie Skuteczność w szybkim, zmiennym środowisku przy dużej skali operacyjnej
